title: Effective descent of an ordered log tower through its centers
statement:
Let $u:(U,N)\to(X,M)$ be a surjective strict etale morphism of locally Noetherian fs log schemes [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $S=(U_n\to\cdots\to U_0=U)$ be a finite saturated log blowup tower with nonempty coherent centers $J_i\subset N_i$, together with an ordered isomorphism $\theta:p_1^*S\simeq p_2^*S$ of its uncontracted recursive pullbacks on $R=U\times_XU$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-trf-strict-etale-log-blowup-procedure]. Assume $\theta$ preserves the actual centers, is the identity on the diagonal, and satisfies $\theta_{23}\theta_{12}=\theta_{13}$ on the triple fiber product. Use the small-site universe convention [def-weil-size-convention].

There exists a finite saturated log blowup tower $B=(X_n\to\cdots\to X_0=X)$ of length $n$, with nonempty coherent centers $I_i\subset M_i$ and an isomorphism $u^*B\simeq S$ inducing $\theta$, without deleting any stage. Each $X_i$ is locally Noetherian and fs. The isomorphisms identify $U_i$ with the scheme-theoretic pullbacks $U\times_XX_i$ and the level-$i$ overlap with $U_i\times_{X_i}U_i$. Under these identifications the ideal is characterized, for every etale $V\to X_i$, by
$$I_i(V)=\{m\in M_i(V):m|_{V\times_{X_i}U_i}\in J_i(V\times_{X_i}U_i)\}.$$
This is an ideal subsheaf of $M_i$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets], whose restriction is $J_i$; it is the unique such subideal. Nonempty finite local generators for $J_i$ are also local generators for the restriction of $I_i$. Each $X_{i+1}$ is the universal saturated blowup of $I_i$, and its strict etale restriction is the given blowup of $J_i$, compatibly with $\theta$. Each $U_i\to X_i$ is surjective strict etale. If every $J_i$ is proper, then every $I_i$ is proper, so $B$ is contracted. Length zero and the empty base are allowed.

source.place: VIII 3.3.7--3.3.10, pp.107--108 and the initial descent assertion of proof of 3.3.15, p.109: effectivity expanded by descending each actual ideal and constructing its universal blowup.

proof.text: Induct on the number $i$ of reconstructed arrows. The invariant is a tower over $X$ through $X_i$, with locally Noetherian fs levels, a center-preserving identification of its full pullback through level $i$ with the given tower, and agreement with $\theta$ through that level. For $i=0$ take $X_0=X$, $U_0=U$ and the given strict cover; the ordered datum is the identity at its initial level. By the first assertion of [lem-trf-log-tower-cover-synchronization], full pullbacks of any reconstructed prefix are scheme-theoretic pullbacks and give surjective strict etale maps $u_i:U_i\to X_i$. The fibre-product universal property identifies its level-$i$ overlap with $U_i\times_{X_i}U_i$: both represent $R\times_X X_i$. Thus preservation of the next actual center by $\theta_i$ means equality of the two restrictions of $J_i$ inside the common log sheaf on this overlap. Work on the small sites in the stipulated universes.

source.place: VIII proof of 3.3.15, p.109, initial descent assertion, expanded as ordered induction; 3.3.10, p.108.

proof.text: For $i<n$, define $I_i(V)$ by the formula in the statement. Restrictions preserve membership since $J_i$ is a subsheaf. If sections of $I_i$ on an etale covering $\{V_a\to V\}$ agree, first glue them in $M_i(V)$. Their restrictions to $V\times_{X_i}U_i$ belong locally to $J_i$, on the covering $\{V_a\times_{X_i}U_i\}$; the sheaf equalizer for $J_i$ puts the glued restriction in $J_i$. This proves the sheaf axiom for $I_i$, including uniqueness, since $I_i\subset M_i$. If $m\in I_i(V)$ and $a\in M_i(V)$, then $(ma)|_{V\times_{X_i}U_i}$ belongs to $J_i$ because $J_i$ is an ideal. Hence $I_i$ is an ideal subsheaf, not merely an abstract descended sheaf.

source.place: Definition 00VM (definition-sheaf-sets), equalizer condition; applied to the log-ideal subsheaf of ILO VIII 3.3.7.

proof.text: We check $I_i|_{U_i}=J_i$ on every etale $W\to U_i$. Strictness identifies $M_i(W)$ with $N_i(W)$. For $m\in J_i(W)$ pull back along $W\times_{X_i}U_i\to W$. The two maps to $U_i$ (the specified map from $W$, and the second projection) induce a map to $U_i\times_{X_i}U_i$. The center equality from Step 1 says that this pulled-back section lies in $J_i$ viewed through the second map. This is exactly the condition $m\in I_i(W)$. Conversely, if $m\in I_i(W)$, restrict that condition along the section $W\to W\times_{X_i}U_i$ supplied by $W\to U_i$ to obtain $m\in J_i(W)$. For any other ideal subsheaf $K\subset M_i$ restricting to $J_i$, the sheaf equalizer on the cover $V\times_{X_i}U_i\to V$ gives $m\in K(V)$ exactly when its restriction belongs to $J_i$. Thus $K=I_i$.

source.place: VIII 3.3.7 and proof of 3.3.15, p.109, actual-ideal descent expanded sectionwise; sheaf equalizer as Stacks 00VM.

proof.text: Choose a strict etale chart cover of $U_i$ on which the coherent ideal $J_i$ has a finite nonempty set of chart generators. By Step 3 the restriction of $I_i$ on each of these same charts is exactly $J_i$. The composite charts over $X_i$ are strict etale and cover $X_i$, since $u_i$ is a surjective strict etale cover. These are therefore coherent charts for $I_i$ in the definition of a nonempty coherent log ideal. This also proves the assertion about the very same local generators, without asserting that a generator descends to a global section of $M_i$.

source.place: VIII 3.3.7, p.107: etale-local coherent charts for log ideals.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-coherent-log-ideal-chart-construction] to $(X_i,M_i),I_i$ and take its fs universal principalization as $X_{i+1}\to X_i$. Its strict etale restriction is the universal saturated blowup of $J_i$ by Step 3 and the strict-restriction clause of that lemma. Both it and the specified $U_{i+1}$ have this universal property, so the unique factor maps in the two directions are inverse (each composite is the unique endomorphism over the base). Extend the prefix identification by this isomorphism. The first assertion of [lem-trf-log-tower-cover-synchronization], applied to the enlarged full tower, identifies $U_{i+1}$ with $U\times_X X_{i+1}$ and makes its map to $X_{i+1}$ surjective strict etale. Since $U_{i+1}$ is locally Noetherian, [lem-trf-etale-local-noetherian-descent] makes $X_{i+1}$ locally Noetherian. The chart construction already makes it fs.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8--3.3.10, pp.107--108, and proof of 3.3.15, p.109; local Noetherianity via Stacks 034C (lemma-Noetherian-local-fppf).

proof.text: The new isomorphism realizes the specified datum as well. On $R$, the two restrictions of $X_{i+1}$ are saturated blowups of the same actual ideal after the already verified identification at level $i$. The map induced by the reconstructed tower and the given $\theta_{i+1}$ are both morphisms between these universal objects over that identified base. Uniqueness in the saturated blowup universal property makes the two morphisms equal. The center-preservation hypothesis for $\theta$ now supplies the equality of the next two centers needed in Step 1. Hence the invariant extends from $i$ to $i+1$. Repeating Steps 2--6 exactly $n$ times constructs $B$ of length $n$ and its ordered pullback isomorphism inducing all of $\theta$. The fibre-product identification in Step 1 applies at every completed level; no stage has been removed.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8--3.3.10, pp.107--108: uniqueness of universal blowup maps and recursive tower pullback; descent assertion in proof of 3.3.15.

proof.text: If $I_i=M_i$, restriction and Step 3 give $J_i=N_i$. Thus every proper $J_i$ forces $I_i$ proper, so the output is contracted under that additional hypothesis. This uses properness of the ideal, not whether its blowup morphism is an isomorphism: a proper principal ideal is retained. When $n=0$ the base case itself is the required tower. When $X$ is empty all $U_i$ and reconstructed levels are empty, the same sheaf formulas and universal constructions apply, and they still retain the specified length. There is only the whole ideal on an empty level, so if all centers are additionally required proper, the empty-base case necessarily has $n=0$.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8--3.3.10, p.108: contraction removes precisely whole-monoid centers; zero length and empty-base cases of the definitions.

proof_origin.place: VIII 3.3.7--3.3.10, pp.107--108; proof of 3.3.15, p.109. Explicit sectionwise ideal descent and ordered reconstruction supplied by Q15.
